## 2. GBM calibration (annualised)
| Dataset | Method | μ | SE(μ) | σ | g = μ − σ²/2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shiller 1926–2023 (monthly avg) | monthly MLE | 0.109 | 0.016 | 0.153 | 0.097 |
| Shiller 1988–2023 (monthly avg) | monthly MLE | 0.109 | 0.021 | 0.124 | 0.102 |
| Yahoo 1988–2023 (month-end) | monthly MLE | 0.113 | 0.025 | 0.148 | 0.102 |
| Yahoo 1988–2024 (month-end) | monthly MLE | 0.117 | 0.024 | 0.147 | 0.106 |
| Shiller 1926–2023 | annual log returns | 0.113 | 0.019 | 0.185 | 0.096 |

Shiller prices are monthly *averages*: monthly σ is biased low by ≈√(2/3) (Working 1960). The annual-return estimator removes this; it is used for the long-run calibration.

## 3. Are monthly log returns i.i.d. normal (the GBM assumption)?
| Dataset | skew | excess kurt | Jarque–Bera | lag-1 autocorr (±2SE) | P(< −3σ) obs / normal | worst month |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shiller 1926–2023 | -0.53 | 12.15 | 7253 (5% crit 6.0) | 0.268 (±0.058) | 1.45% / 0.13% | -26.2% |
| Yahoo 1988–2024 | -0.71 | 1.38 | 73 (5% crit 6.0) | -0.009 (±0.095) | 0.68% / 0.13% | -16.8% |

Worst historical start months for invest-first (vs payoff-first): 1935-10 (-50,642), 1935-12 (-49,713), 1936-01 (-48,530)
Invest-first lost in 32.2% of windows; these windows overlap heavily (≈4 independent 20-year periods), so treat this as descriptive.

## 5. Breakeven loan APR (P(invest-first wins) = 50%)
Volatility-drag prediction r* ≈ μ − σ²/2 = 0.096 (long-run calibration; nominal, continuous)
- GBM long-run: breakeven APR ≈ 0.095
- History rolling: breakeven APR ≈ 0.108
- Bootstrap: breakeven APR ≈ 0.101
